citations.review_text: Coming from BioShock 2, this was a major disappointment. I will admit that the game is visually beautiful, the art direction is excellent, and the overall experience is smoother than in previous titles. However, it suffers from severe mechanical simplification, including the standard Call of Duty-style two-weapon formula. The story has the appearance of depth through its multiple-worlds plot, but is ultimately thematically shallow. 4/10 as a standalone game; 2/10 as a BioShock title.

[h1]A genuinely great game that only leaves you wishing for a little more.[/h1]

[b]Executive Summary:[/b]
I definitely enjoyed my time with [i]BioShock Infinite[/i]. While looking at the early gameplay demos and concept art makes you realize it could have been even grander, the final product we got is still a very good game. My main takeaway is simply: "It's fine, but it could have been even better."

[h2]Combat & Gunplay[/h2]
Gunplay is a very important factor for me in games, and I thoroughly enjoyed it here. Compared to the previous [i]BioShock[/i] entries, the shooting mechanics finally feel satisfying and have a great impact. The combat overall is incredibly fun. My only real complaint in this department is the two-weapon limit; restricting the player to carrying only two guns at a time felt like a completely unnecessary limitation.

Additionally, Elizabeth is an amazing companion. I absolutely loved how she was implemented mechanically, especially her role and assistance during combat encounters.

[h2]World Design & Story[/h2]
The locations are quite unique, and I really liked the visual direction of the world. However, it is a shame that some elements from the concept art didn't make the final cut. Specifically, the Toy Maker's factory—I really love personalized locations that reflect specific characters, and I deeply regret that this was left out of the game.

As for the story, it is a bit hard to evaluate based on general consensus. I know some people complain that the plot gets convoluted and doesn't make sense, but personally, it made sense to me. I had no problems with it and thought it was a fine narrative. The Vox Populi storyline was also good, though, much like other aspects of the game, it felt like it had the potential to be fleshed out a bit more.

[h2]The Weakest Link: Comstock House[/h2]

The gun play and usage of the Vigors/Plasmids have aged well. The movement is mostly good minus the occasional getting stuck on nothing and having to jump to move again. For those with HiDPi setups like 4K, go into the config settings in the steam game folder and change the config UI scaling from 0.0 to 1.0 to fix the small UI issues. The performance was almost perfect on 4K maxed settings. I only noticed some texture issues where it couldnt make its mind up on if it wanted to use the low or high res texture and kept cycling between them quickly. 

The story and ending is highly contested; so I would say I enjoyed the story and appreciate how a team could come up with it but I think they could have tied it better to the other entries in the series to be more powerful. 

Overall, grab it on sale and give it a go for a fun time.

citations.review_text: One of the most emotional endings of all time in gaming. There's definitely some sections that could have been better, like the final defense section and just going back and forth between the factories in the second act. However, the gameplay and presentation still hold up after all these years. If a mod could remove the two weapon limit and change the resource management to upgrade all weapons, would easily be a 10/10.

Wow, couldnt have loved it more.

Columbia is easily one of the most beautiful places I've ever explored in a game, and I loved just taking my time to soak it all in. The gameplay was a blast, but the story and the bond between Booker and Elizabeth are what really made this unforgettable. That ending left me completely speechless. I genuinely didn't know whether to smile or just sit there in disbelief, and I was feeling both at the same time, I was amazed by how good it was.

My only complaint is being limited to two weapons. I really wish we could carry at least three. Other than that, absolute peak.

Worst of the trilogy. Two weapon limitation is the dumbest idea ever, and results in a pretty poor 'shooter.' 

Story is all over the place, trying to appease to many audiences at once, and in turn falls apart trying to haphazardly tie everything back to Bioshock 1, for some reason, while no where in the entire game was their anything calling back to that, and if there was, it was poorly done. Definitely the weakest narrative of the bunch.

citations.review_text: Mouse sensitivity is a slider with no number. You just gotta vibe it out i guess

5/5 - a masterpiece and if you had only 1 bioshock game to play then play this one and it's DLCs  burial at the sea 1+2 - difficulty played: hard

BioShock Infinite works because it trusts you to figure things out no map but i end up at the right place always. 

The story only makes complete sense at the end, which makes the payoff hit harder. It feels like a prequel to the first BioShock even though it released last. Combat is fast and clean 5/5, though the weapon zoom is awkward and you will need to rebind keys. Getting lost happens once in a blue moon instead of constantly, and the game never holds your hand — I did not know the N key showed the path until the DLC. Columbia is stunning, the atmosphere is perfect, and the two leads carry everything. BioShock 2 has a story too that you have to figure out but Infinite is simply better written — clearer, more polished story, and unforgettable.

citations.review_text:
Main story review: 8/10
[+] Positives:
Great world building, great graphics, fun action, Elizabeth.

[-] Negatives:
Lack of bosses, too many weapons without meaningful difference, NO MANUAL OR QUICK SAVE, Vigor (spells) upgrades are too expensive, ending with a completely unnecessary twist, achievements that ruin the game if you try to get in first run.

If you want to have best experience don't try to complete achievements on first run. Don't even look at them. Don't go after every penny, don't search every cabinet and drawer like I did. Look around, breathe environment in, listen audio logs, beat the enemies in your style, understand the story and motives of characters.

Immerse yourself in. That's the way.

I have a bone to pick with Bioshock: Infinite, I think it's hugely overrated and gets way more praise than it deserves. After recently playing through the entire Bioshock franchise on PC, I can confidently say this game is the weakest in the series. 

We'll start with the good, because there is some. Columbia is beautiful, the setting starts off compelling, there's a recipe for something good here. There's auto-saving too, which is great if you don't know what a quick-save is. Sky-hooks are fun, at least for a little while. There's plasmids, or vigors if you want to insist they're different. You can eat food straight from the trash while Elizabeth yaps about how much she loves Paris. You can be certain you'll never miss what's going on in the story as every single character including Booker loves to loudly narrate every single inner thought to the player.

Now onto what I don't like, if it wasn't obvious there's a *lot*. First and foremost: This is NOT an immersive sim, its a bog-standard 2013 cover/shield shooter. Yep, you have the Halo shield, can only carry two weapons. Plasmids were dumbed down to a kindergarten level, and fun imaginative weapon upgrades have been turned into "25% more damage." Manual saving is gone, now you only get auto-saves and you have to deal with it. The DLC loads you up with free upgrades right at the start of the game that feels like cheating if you take them, not to mention the "golden gun" upgrades that look awful and make your weapons stronger for some reason.

I think what irritates me most of all is how the open landscapes and enemy design lead to some of the most boring shooter gameplay I've experienced in a long time. The world is big and open, which sounds great on paper except all of the enemies are some variation of "guy with a gun" that shoots you with hitscan from far away as soon as they see you and chips your shield and health down. There is no way to avoid damage in this game outside of cover, which there is often very li…

[h3]Title: Bioshock Infinite[/h3] 
(DLC REQUIRED FOR 100%)

Summary: Atmospheric fps game

Personal notes: Bioshock Infinite is the third entry in the Bioshock series, this time being a prequel that takes place about 50 years before the events of the first game. Infinite also leaves behind the underwater city of Rapture and instead takes place in Columbia, a massive floating city in the clouds. You play as Booker, a detective tasked with finding and returning a woman named Elizabeth to New York. Sounds simple enough right...watch out for birds! I played the first two Bioshock games on the xbox growing up but skipped Infinite and decided to go back and play through all three and honestly, I had a blast. The gameplay of Infinite is a lot faster and "loose" than the previous entries which in addition to the increased mobility made combat feel fun and chaotic. I felt like I enjoyed the gunplay and speed of the combat more but was left a little dissapointed with the Vigors, Columbia's version of plasmids. I felt like they were less varied and only a few were really viable. Plus I was not a big fan of only being able to carry two weapons in comparision to the wheel but I did get pretty used to it after a while. The world design is once again incredible. Columbia is very impressive visually and exploring the city was very rewarding. They go from the sea to the sky but still manage to create a beautiful and engaging world that invites you to explore. The story of Infinite is also very strong despite having mixed opinions on the end and DLC endings. citations.review_text:
Very good of course. The DLC is a great addition especially part II. Great fun.
Runs smoothly on old PCs.

Played this game when it first launched and still come back to it every few years on different platforms. I really enjoy the setting, music, gameplay, and the Lutece characters.

Because the graphics aren't hyper realistic it doesn't really look all that dated and the gameplay is still smooth. With my humble setup I hit 180 FPS on 1080p, and the game runs really well on Steam deck as well and doesn't necessarily feel like a battery killer. However, if you wanna play in 4k on a larger monitor you may want to consider installing a mod to increase the size of the text and HUD, it's really really tiny otherwise.

cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight navigational bugs with companion pathing and progression-blocking freezes near the end.

claims.claim: Reviewers report movement issues where Elizabeth's hitbox or pathing can block the player and cause them to get stuck or trapped in certain spots.

citations.review_text:
When I first played this game 10 years ago in 2016 I walked away from it not caring much for it. I couldn't really grasp how it was still Bioshock, a sentiment that seems common. There were completely new characters, locations, and history. A lot of change for seemingly no reason. But without the blinders of nostalgia, and an observant mind, you eventually see and understand the reasons. Especially if you actually play the DLC which I never did all those years ago. There may still be some confusing details if you don't think or learn enough about it, but they do a pretty great job of tying things together.

As for some practical critique of the game, there's not much to complain about other than a few minor things. The plasmids (vigors) I remember being disappointed by when I first played, I like them more now but overall I didn't enjoy very much of them. I was also not fond of the new limit of 2 carried weapons. Elizabeth follows you around to aid you which is cool, but she has a hitbox that can block you from moving, that could be done better. I've restarted sections from getting stuck in some places. They also make her teleport around depending on her distance from you and where you're facing so that she is guaranteed enough screen time. It is very common to turn and catch her before it happens and her body is doing some weird contortionism. There is actually one big flaw where the game runs at a staggeringly slow speed if your fps is too high, but it can be fixed with forced vsync and/or the built-in frame lock setting. 

Overall great experience, glad I finally saw it all make sense, might finally play the Remastered prequels too.

Idk man it still feels like a good game after all this time. Modern day Elizabeth's pathing has me aiming down my sights at her on purpose to get her to move and there's some weird spots where you just get caught and stop moving for some reason but overall this is still a neat little game. 

if you don't think too hard about it

I've got my issues with Infinite. It was my introduction to the Bioshock series as a whole, after beating it I went back and played 1 and 2. As a standalone game, I'd recommend it.

There'll be spoilers ahead.

However, if you've played either Bioshock, Bioshock 2, or both, I can't. 
They did nail the aesthetics. It looks very pretty. I see the concept they went for... until [spoiler] you hop into a tear in reality to get weapons back for the Vox Populi. [/spoiler]
After that, the entire plot fell apart. Why would [spoiler] Daisy [/spoiler] need you to bring those back when you aren't even [spoiler] in the same reality anymore? [/spoiler] In this one, Booker's [spoiler] dead [/spoiler]. Your objective was back in [spoiler] reality 1 [/spoiler]. We never end back up there.

The plot holes just keep going from there on.

The combat is ok. I do not like only being able to hold onto 2 guns, though. I get it, people didn't like cycling through every weapon (looking at you, camera) in the first game, but at least give us 4 slots. Sometimes more than two weapons are needed. What if i'm holding a machine gun and a pistol, but also need a rifle or a shotgun? Leaving behind a favorite weapon sucks, especially if you've upgraded it.

Speaking of upgrades, you better be ready to loot absolutely everything, because unlike having a currency for plasmids, your vigors will cost money to upgrade, too. Even after wiping out every enemy in one area, looting every corpse and searching every desk/barrel/trash can, I still couldn't afford a single upgrade once I got to the second vending machine. Or the first.

You also can't carry any health kits. You're given a shield to balance that out. Every consumable must be consumed then and there. Apparently, Booker can hold onto two guns, but can't carry a med kit. It just doesn't make sense. Elizabeth tossing you items later on can help a little, but where th…
